sections.text:
Philippians is a warm letter of thanks and encouragement, written from prison. Paul thanks the church for a gift, reports that his imprisonment has helped spread the good news, and urges them to stand together.

At its heart is a poem about Christ, who humbled himself to death on a cross and was raised to the highest place (2:5 to 11). Paul counts everything else as loss compared with knowing Christ. Joy runs through the whole letter.

Philippi was a Roman colony in Macedonia, and its church was the first Paul founded in Europe (Acts 16). Where Paul was imprisoned when he wrote is debated: Rome, Ephesus and Caesarea are the main proposals.

The poem in chapter 2 is one of the earliest statements of who Christians believe Jesus to be, and much has been written on what it means that he emptied himself. The line about being able to do all things through Christ (4:13) is often quoted about achievement. In its setting it is about being content in hunger and in plenty.
